title: Exec Brief Mini Playbook + Risk Heatmap
content:
Purpose: Quick, repeatable one-page briefing and an email-first quarterly recap that CSMs can hand to executive sponsors. Focus: surface strategic outcomes, risks with a compact heatmap, and a short renewal health tracker + asks.

Who this is for: executive sponsors (VP+/Head of Product/Engineering), CSMs prepping for 20–30 minute sponsor check-ins, and AEs prepping renewals.

How to use: fill the TL;DR, paste 3 metrics, tick the heatmap, add 1–2 asks. Keep the meeting to 20 minutes: 5 min TL;DR, 8 min key outcomes & risks, 5 min decisions/asks, 2 min next steps.

Template: Exec Brief (one page / email body)
- Subject: [Customer] QBR snapshot — 90 day outcomes and executive asks
- TL;DR (1–2 sentences): "In Q1 we saw X: [high-level outcome]. Our top priority next quarter: [one-line objective]."
- Top 3 metrics (last 90 days):
  - Production requests/day: [num] (QoQ % change)
  - 95th percentile latency: [ms] (SLO: [ms])
  - Cost per 1k tokens or cost per inference: [$/unit] (trend arrow)
- Strategic wins (bullets, up to 3): short descriptors + impact (revenue/ops/latency)\- Example: "Reduced tail latency for chat flow by 30% via cache tuning — improved conversion on checkout flows (~2% uplift)"
- Open risks & mitigation (brief) — see Risk Heatmap below
- Renewal health score (0–100): [score] + rationale (usage, NPS, roadmap fit)
- Asks for executive sponsor (pick 1–2): e.g., expedite access to 3rd party data, approve Dedicated capacity pilot, champion internal data sharing with infra team
- Next steps & owners (explicit dates): owner — action — due date

Risk Heatmap (compact): rate each axis 1 (low) to 5 (critical) then compute center-of-mass to get Low/Medium/High
Axes: Business Impact | Technical Risk | Timeline Sensitivity
- Example scoring for a risk item: "Fresh model variance in production" -> Business Impact: 3, Technical Risk: 4, Timeline: 4 => composite: HIGH

Quick heatmap legend:
- Low: composite <= 3.0 (monitor)
- Medium: composite 3.1–3.9 (action plan + owner)
- High: composite >= 4.0 (exec attention + mitigation)

Common risk tokens to check (checkbox list for CSM):
- Model quality regressions on top customer prompts
- Cost spikes above committed capacity
- Latency SLO breaches (>=3 incidents in rolling 30d)
- Data residency / legal gating for Private deployment
- API quota exhaustion during peak events

Renewal health tracker (compact): place in the email as 1-line bullets; maintain full tracker in spreadsheet linked below.
- Contract term: [mm/yy]
- Current commitment vs usage: [committed GPU hours / actual usage] (trend)
- Executive sponsor engagement: [high/medium/low] (last touch: YYYY-MM-DD)
- Risk level: [low|medium|high]
- Primary renewal blocker: [pricing | security | technical | roadmap fit | other]

Suggested meeting agenda (20 min):
1) 0–5 min: TL;DR + customer business context (CSM)
2) 5–13 min: Key metrics and strategic wins (CSM + Solutions Eng)
3) 13–18 min: Top 2 risks + mitigation ask (CSM)
4) 18–20 min: Decisions / Exec asks & commitments (AE / sponsor)

Customer-facing Qtr Recap Email (short):
- Subject: [Customer name] — Q[X] recap & next steps
- Greeting: "Hi [Exec], quick recap from our quarterly review — highlights and two asks below."
- Body bullets: 3 wins, 1 risk, 1 metric, 1 ask + calendar link for 15-minute follow-up
- Closing: "Thanks — would love your quick OK on the two asks so we can prioritise resources."

Sample recap email (draft):
Hi [First],
Thanks again for your time on [date]. Quick recap: 
• Win: Reduced inference cost by 18% via quantization profile change (Ops + Solutions)
• Win: Increased serving availability to 99.95% (rolling 30d)
• Metric: Avg daily inferences up 42% QoQ
• Risk: Need Dedicated pool approval to sustain expected growth — without it we expect 2–4% latency regression under Black Friday-like loads
Ask: Can you confirm an internal sponsor for capacity approval by [date]?
Link: [calendar link to schedule 15m follow-up]
Thanks,
[CSM name]

Implementation notes / CSM checklist (practical)
- Fill the one-pager 48 hours before the QBR and share with sponsor 24 hours before meeting\- Pin 1–2 engineering/funding asks — avoid laundry lists\- Attach 1-pg appendix with two sample prompts and baseline outputs if quality is a concern\- Include a short log of incidents (last 90d) with links to internal postmortems

Examples of good asks (CSMs should adapt to customer maturity):
- "Approve Dedicated GPU pilot (2 months) to stabilize latency for peak events"
- "Greenlight limited token-budget increase to cover forecasted growth (Q3)"
- "Assign infra owner to unblock cross-team network ACL change for Private deployment"

Notes on tone: keep exec-grade language (outcomes, dollars, availability) — avoid technical deep dives unless sponsor asks. Bring a Solutions Engineer for 8–10 minutes for critical technical asks.

Appendix: Quick internal links to attach when sending
- Full renewal tracker (Sheets): [link-placeholder]
- Recent postmortem(s): [PM-XXXX]
- Performance dashboard: Redwood Console -> Customer route -> 95th latency chart (link)
- Feature roadmap item: GH-1337 (brief description)

Open questions / TODOs (for CSM to resolve before send)
- Confirm exact revenue/ARR attribution for the feature that showed uplift (finance)
- Get AE to confirm negotiation margin target for renewal (sales)
- Validate Dedicated capacity cost estimate with infra (eng/infra)

Notes from last usage: "Customer has three product teams using API — two are in rapid expansion, one is in testing mode. Sponsor wants low-effort/low-risk proposal (short pilot)."

Versioning / changelog
- 2025-02-14: Initial draft by Priya (skeleton + heatmap logic)
- 2025-02-28: Added sample email and checklist (Marco)
- 2025-03-05: Clarified renewal tracker fields and added linked artifacts (Eleni)

Quick content repurpose ideas
- Turn TL;DR into a one-slide executive summary for the QBR deck
- Use the heatmap as a single graphic in the customer-facing recap email (PNG)

End of doc.
